question: A researcher compiled data. Starting sample: 94 readings. Added 4 calibration points. Subtracted 21 for outliers. Subtracted 50 for errors. Multiplied by 2 for verification. Multiplied by 7 for final analysis. How many verified data points?

A charity tracked the total dollars in its silent auction fund throughout gala night, starting with 158 dollars raised before doors opened. During the cocktail hour, 38 more dollars came in. During dinner, 24 more dollars came in. During the live auction, a matching donor multiplied the tracked fund by 7. During dessert, a second matching donor doubled the tracked fund again. A separate raffle at the same gala, unrelated to this fund, brought in 500 dollars. By the end of the night, a large venue bill took 1136 dollars out of the tracked fund. How many dollars were in the silent auction fund by the end of the night?

A school had 94 recorders in its music room, and a grant paid for 62 more. 101 recorders were lent out to pupils for the term. Each recorder still in the room comes with 9 sheets of music in its case. The choir used 430 of those sheets for a concert, and a teacher then printed 27 more. A dozen music stands are kept in the corner, and the room is 12 metres wide. How many sheets of music are in the room?

A bakery started with 83 pastries. For a catering order, production increased 7 times to 581 pastries total. The company delivered 254 pastries for an event, leaving 327. In storage, they found 8 additional pastries forgotten on a shelf. For a special contract, they prepared 6 complete batches of this amount, requiring 2,010 pastries. The bakery has been operating for 25 years (separate context). How many pastries must they prepare for the contract?

A parking garage had 198 cars at the start of the morning. By midday, 173 cars left for a downtown event. An afternoon rush doubled the remaining count. By evening, 78 more cars pulled in for a concert. Overnight, a final wave made the total grow to 4 times its size. How many cars were in the garage by the next morning?

A hospital radio station had 149 records in its cabinet, and a listener donated 69 more. A burst pipe destroyed 197 records. The station then made 7 digital copies of every record that survived. A volunteer added 34 copies from her own collection, a college sent 45, and a local band contributed 35. Half of the cabinet is now taken up by cables. How many copies does the station have?

In the morning the crew laid 6 lines of cable, each 60 fathoms long. In the afternoon they added 5 fathoms at the pier and 69 fathoms along the wall. In the evening they recorded the total in feet, since a fathom is 6 feet. How many feet of cable did they record?

Grandma Rosa's classroom library began the semester with 133 books on its shelves. She donated 43 books to a sister school in need. A publisher then sent 53 brand-new books as a grant reward. When the reading club reorganized, every book on the shelf was matched with 6 duplicate copies for a book fair display, set up with help from a dozen or so volunteers. The fair brought in 24 more donated books afterward. At the end of the semester, 765 books were shipped off to a regional donation center. How many books remained on Rosa's classroom shelves after the shipment?

A card factory stores 173 boxes, and every box holds 9 packs. A short delivery added 61 packs, and a returned order brought back 7 more. Each pack in the store contains 7 cards. Every card comes with 2 stickers sealed inside it. A supplier then sent 26 loose stickers to the same store. How many stickers are in the store altogether?

A farm had 230 liters. They divided by 5 to allocate to sections. They subtracted 37 liters used. They multiplied by 7 to calculate weekly needs. They subtracted 26 liters. Finally, 16 liters were removed for testing. Using the word 'half', between the morning and evening shift, how many liters remain?

Two organizers prepared an event. Starting base: 27 attendees. Multiplied by 8 for projected growth. Added 43 confirmations. Added 66 walk-ups. Multiplied by 9 for table groupings. Added 51 VIP seats. Two organizers coordinated. How many total VIP and regular seats?

A team lead tracked project progress. Starting deliverables: 139. Subtracted 115 for early completion. Added 75 from scope expansion. Added 68 new requirements. Subtracted 147 for descoped work. How many final deliverables planned?
A store started with 45 items. They removed 37. They multiplied by 5. They added 16. They added 10 more. How many items does the store have (as a final count)?

Hana set up a lemonade stand in the morning with 104 paper cups, and she sold 41 cups before ten and another 18 by noon. In the afternoon she sold 26 cups to a passing football team and 15 to a group of joggers, and 1 cup blew away in the wind. Each cup of lemonade cost 2 dollars. In the evening her father brought her a fresh pack of 77 cups. Her brother Kai, who ran a stand across the street, sold fewer cups than Hana all day. How many cups did Hana have at the end of the evening?
A library had 156 books. They divided by 3. They added 51. They added 21. They added 57. There was a dozen distractor books. They multiplied by 7. How many books?

A farmer began with 39 vegetables from the garden. He multiplied his harvest 6 times through expansion to 234. He then grew this amount 5 times larger through additional plots, reaching 1,170 vegetables. He sold 769 at the market, leaving 401. He donated 392 to a food bank. He added 71 to his personal storage. He then packaged the remainder into 4 equal shipments. His farm covers 80 acres (not counted). How many vegetables are in each shipment?

A parcel depot began Tuesday with 124 parcels on the sorting bench. A late van brought in 69 more. Then 5 parcels were pulled out as damaged, and 44 went off on the first delivery round. Every parcel still on the bench contains 3 separately wrapped items. The drivers cover 87 kilometres on a typical round and log their journeys in minutes rather than hours. How many wrapped items are on the bench?
A student had 206 items. They added 8 items. They tripled them. They multiplied by 8 times. They removed 707 items. Someone had a dozen items. How many items?

A library starts its day with 157 books in the processing queue. They process 116 returns. They receive 53 new donations. They process another 19 returns. They remove 46 damaged books. The library director has been in charge for 25 years. How many books remain in the processing queue?

A store started with 150 items. They added 16 items. They added 16 more items. They added 66 items. They added 50 items. They added 78 items. A partner store had 300 items. Converting to hundreds, how many items are there?

Nora begins the week with 204 stickers in her album, while her friend Beth has only 90 stickers. Nora attends a swap meet where every sticker she brought gets doubled by a special two-for-one trade. She then loses 334 stickers when a page falls out of her album and blows away. Her aunt gives her 77 replacement stickers, and she finds 23 more stuck to the bottom of her bag. Finally, a sticker club multiplies her whole collection ninefold as a reward for a puzzle she solved. How many stickers does Nora have now?

Camille's charity jar held $92 after the weekend bake sale. She split the money evenly into 4 identical envelopes for different charities and kept only one envelope for the local shelter. She then spent $1 on a stamp to mail a thank-you note. A generous donor added $14 more to the shelter's envelope. A matching sponsor then turned every dollar in the envelope into 9 dollars, and a final grant turned each of those into 8 dollars, a process the shelter director said took about 90 minutes, or an hour and a half, from start to finish. How much money was in Camille's envelope after the final grant was applied?

Two consultants, Lisa and Tom, compared projects. Tom had 98 active projects. He added 77 new initiatives. He subtracted 42 completed. He added 52 proposals. He multiplied by 5 for scaling. He added 70 contingency projects. Converting to days needed at a dozen per day, how many days of work?
A count started at 239. By morning, it tripled. By midday, 57 were added. By afternoon, 56 more arrived. By evening, 80 were added. His colleague had 150. How many (tripling as a unit grouping)?

Hugo bakes 27 shortbread rounds on each of the 5 trays he owns. A neighbour gave him 80 more rounds for the village sale. His sister Mia contributed 45, although Mia had baked fewer rounds than Hugo. The village hall has 96 chairs. Hugo then repeated his whole collection 5 times over, so that every stall at the fair could have the same amount. How many shortbread rounds did Hugo end up with?
